questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of the $Mn^{2+}$ ion (Z = 25), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^5$. Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The four other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. All eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $19.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 25 - 19.40 = 5.60$ and $10 \times 5.60 = 56$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For a $Cu^{2+}$ ion (Z = 29, configuration $[Ar]3d^9$), find the effective nuclear charge on one 3d electron, multiply it by 10, and report the integer result.
questions.explanation: The eight other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.80$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $20.80$, so $Z_{eff} = 29 - 20.80 = 8.20$ and $10 \times 8.20 = 82$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of the $Cr^{3+}$ ion (Z = 24), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^3$, after accounting for all shielding?
questions.explanation: The two other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $0.70$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $18.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 24 - 18.70 = 5.30$. Ignoring the 3d partners gives 4.00, reporting total screening gives 18.70, and screening the inner shells at 0.85 gives 6.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of an $Fe^{2+}$ ion (Z = 26, configuration $[Ar]3d^6$) is screened from one 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The five other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.75$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$ in total. Total screening is $19.75$, and $19.75/26 = 0.7596$, which is 76 percent after rounding.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 3d electron of a neutral titanium atom (Z = 22), whose configuration is $[Ar]3d^2 4s^2$.
questions.explanation: The other 3d electron screens $0.35$. The eighteen electrons in the 1s to 3p shells screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$, and the 4s electrons screen nothing for a 3d electron in this scheme. Total screening is $18.35$, so $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.35 = 3.65$. Ignoring the 3d partner gives 4.00, reporting total screening gives 18.35, and screening the inner shells at 0.85 gives 6.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge of a 1s electron in a beryllium ion with only two electrons, $Be^{2+}$ (Z = 4). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The other 1s electron is the only partner, and it screens $0.30$. So $Z_{eff} = 4 - 0.30 = 3.70$, and $10 \times 3.70 = 37$. Using a 0.35 partner screening instead of 0.30 would be a common slip for 1s electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a $Li^{+}$ ion (Z = 3) is screened from its only 1s partner electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent, given that the ion carries two electrons?
questions.explanation: The single 1s partner screens $0.30$. The screened fraction is $0.30/3 = 0.10$, or 10 percent, which is the whole-number result.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In a Moseley-type relation the square root of the X-ray frequency equals 6 times (Z minus 2), in chosen units. A line has a square-root frequency of 96 units. What is the atomic number of the emitting element?
questions.explanation: Dividing the square-root frequency by 6 gives $Z - 2 = 96/6 = 16$. Adding 2 gives $Z = 18$, which corresponds to argon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Pauling electronegativities are 0.93 for Na, 1.31 for Mg and 1.61 for Al. What is the mean electronegativity of these three elements, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The sum is $0.93 + 1.31 + 1.61 = 3.85$. Dividing by 3 gives $3.85/3 = 1.283$, which rounds to 1.28. Reporting the Mg value alone gives 1.31, reporting the Al value gives 1.61, and averaging only Na and Al gives 1.27.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3p electron of the $Ca^{2+}$ ion (Z = 20), which carries eighteen electrons in its ground state, $[Ar]$.
questions.explanation: The seven other 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, so $Z_{eff} = 20 - 11.25 = 8.75$. Copying the $K^{+}$ value gives 7.75, ignoring the 2s/2p shell gives 15.55, and reporting total screening gives 11.25.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What percentage of the nuclear charge of a $Cu^{2+}$ ion (Z = 29) is screened from one 3d electron by all the other electrons, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: Total screening is $2.80 + 18.00 = 20.80$, from the eight partner 3d electrons ($0.35$ each) and the eighteen inner electrons ($1.00$ each). The screened fraction is $20.80/29 = 0.7172$, which rounds to 72 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: What is the difference between the 3d effective nuclear charges of $Fe^{3+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^5$) and $Fe^{2+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^6$), to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: For $Fe^{2+}$ the five partner 3d electrons give $5 \times 0.35 = 1.75$, so $Z_{eff} = 26 - 19.75 = 6.25$. For $Fe^{3+}$ the four partners give $1.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 26 - 19.40 = 6.60$. The difference is $6.60 - 6.25 = 0.35$. Doubling the difference gives 0.70, quoting the group term gives 1.75, and quoting the $Fe^{3+}$ value gives 6.60.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Find the effective nuclear charge felt by one 1s electron of a neutral helium atom (Z = 2), multiply it by 10, and give the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The partner 1s electron screens $0.30$, so $Z_{eff} = 2 - 0.30 = 1.70$. Multiplying by 10 gives $17$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of a $Ti^{3+}$ ion (Z = 22, $[Ar]3d^1$), multiply it by 10, and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The single 3d electron has no 3d partners, so only the eighteen inner electrons screen, giving $18.00$. Then $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.00 = 4.00$, and $10 \times 4.00 = 40$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a $V^{2+}$ ion (Z = 23, $[Ar]3d^3$). Multiply the value by 10 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The two other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $0.70$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$ in total. Total screening is $18.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 23 - 18.70 = 4.30$ and $10 \times 4.30 = 43$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 3d effective nuclear charges of these ions. I. The 3d electrons of $Mn^{2+}$ feel a lower value than those of $Fe^{2+}$. II. The 3d electrons of $Cu^{2+}$ feel a higher value than those of $Fe^{2+}$. III. The 3d electrons of $Cr^{3+}$ feel a higher value than those of $Mn^{2+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Mn^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 5.60$ and $Fe^{2+}$ gives 6.25, so I is true. $Cu^{2+}$ gives 8.20, so II is true. $Cr^{3+}$ gives 5.30, which is lower than $Mn^{2+}$ at 5.60, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider these aqueous stability statements about transition metal ions. I. $Mn^{2+}$ is more stable than $Mn^{3+}$. II. $Cr^{3+}$ is more stable than $Cr^{2+}$. III. $Cr^{2+}$ is more stable than $Cr^{3+}$. IV. $Co^{2+}$ is more stable than $Co^{3+}$. How many of these four statements are correct?
questions.explanation: $Mn^{2+}$ is the most stable manganese ion in water, so I is true. $Cr^{2+}$ is a strong reducing agent that is readily oxidised to $Cr^{3+}$, so II is true and III is false. $Co^{3+}$ is a strong oxidant that oxidises water, so IV is true. Three statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the metallic character of Group 14 elements. I. Sn is more metallic than C. II. Pb has a lower first ionisation enthalpy than Sn. III. Ge is a metalloid. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Sn is metallic whereas C is a non-metal, so I is true. Pb (715 kJ/mol) has a higher IE1 than Sn (709 kJ/mol), so II is false. Ge is classified as a metalloid, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the sizes of Group 1 ions. I. $K^{+}$ is larger than $Na^{+}$. II. $Rb^{+}$ is smaller than $K^{+}$. III. $Li^{+}$ is smaller than $Na^{+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $K^{+}$ (138 pm) is larger than $Na^{+}$ (102 pm), so I is true. $Rb^{+}$ (152 pm) is larger than $K^{+}$, so II is false. $Li^{+}$ (76 pm) is smaller than $Na^{+}$, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3d effective nuclear charges of Mn2+ (Z = 25), Fe2+ (Z = 26), Fe3+ (Z = 26), Cr3+ (Z = 24) and Cu2+ (Z = 29). How many of these ions have a 3d effective nuclear charge greater than 6.0?
questions.explanation: The values are Mn2+ 5.60, Fe2+ 6.25, Fe3+ 6.60, Cr3+ 5.30 and Cu2+ 8.20. Only Fe2+, Fe3+ and Cu2+ exceed 6.0, so the count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the successive ionisation enthalpies of iron, IE1 = 762, IE2 = 1562 and IE3 = 2957 kJ/mol. I. IE2 is greater than IE1. II. The ratio IE3/IE2 exceeds 1.8. III. IE2 is smaller than IE1. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: IE2 (1562) is greater than IE1 (762), so I is true. The ratio $2957/1562 = 1.89$ exceeds 1.8, so II is true. IE2 cannot be smaller than IE1 because removing a second electron from a positive ion always costs more, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the Pauling electronegativities of Fe (1.83), Cu (1.90) and Zn (1.65). I. Cu is more electronegative than Fe. II. Zn is less electronegative than Fe. III. Cu is less electronegative than Zn. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Cu (1.90) is more electronegative than Fe (1.83), so I is true. Zn (1.65) is less electronegative than Fe (1.83), so II is true. Cu (1.90) is higher than Zn (1.65), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ and of $Fe^{2+}$. What percentage of the nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ (Z = 25) is screened from its 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The total screening for a 3d electron of $Mn^{2+}$ is $1.40 + 18.00 = 19.40$. The screened fraction is $19.40/25 = 0.776$, which is 77.6 percent and rounds to 78.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by one 4s electron of a neutral titanium atom (Z = 22, $[Ar]3d^2 4s^2$), using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The partner 4s electron screens $0.35$. The ten 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $8.50$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $18.85$, so $Z_{eff} = 22 - 18.85 = 3.15$. Copying the calcium value gives 2.85, quoting the 3d value gives 3.65, and copying the zinc value gives 4.35.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 4s effective nuclear charges of Ca (2.85), Sc (3.00), Ti (3.15), Cr (2.95), Cu (3.70) and Zn (4.35). How many of these have a 4s effective nuclear charge greater than 3.00?
questions.explanation: Ti (3.15), Cu (3.70) and Zn (4.35) exceed 3.00. Ca (2.85), Sc (3.00, which is equal and not greater) and Cr (2.95) do not, so the count is 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the first ionisation enthalpies of some s-block and p-block elements. I. Mg has a higher IE1 than Al. II. Ca has a lower IE1 than Mg. III. Ba has a higher IE1 than Sr. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: Mg (738) is higher than Al (578), so I is true. Ca (590) is lower than Mg (738), so II is true. Ba (503) is lower than Sr (549), so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3p effective nuclear charges of $K^{+}$ (Z = 19), $Ca^{2+}$ (Z = 20), $Cl^{-}$ (Z = 17) and $S^{2-}$ (Z = 16), each treated with usual screening conventions. How many of these four species have a 3p effective nuclear charge above 7.0?
questions.explanation: The values are $K^{+}$ 7.75, $Ca^{2+}$ 8.75, $Cl^{-}$ 5.75 and $S^{2-}$ 4.75. Only $K^{+}$ and $Ca^{2+}$ exceed 7.0, so the count is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{2+}$ to that of $Mn^{2+}$, using the usual screening conventions, to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: $Fe^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 6.25$ and $Mn^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 5.60$. The ratio is $6.25/5.60 = 1.116$, which rounds to 1.12. Inverting the ratio gives 0.90, taking the difference gives 0.65, and assuming equal values gives 1.00.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Mn^{2+}$ is 5.60 and that of $Fe^{2+}$ is 6.25. What is the percentage increase going from the Mn2+ value to the Fe2+ value, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The increase is $6.25 - 5.60 = 0.65$. Relative to the Mn2+ value, this is $0.65/5.60 = 0.116$, or 11.6 percent, which rounds to 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare copper ions and their sizes and stabilities. I. The 3d electrons of $Cu^{2+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{+}$. II. $Cu^{+}$ is more stable than $Cu^{2+}$ in aqueous solution. III. $Cu^{2+}$ is smaller than $Cu^{+}$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Cu^{2+}$ gives $Z_{eff} = 8.20$, while $Cu^{+}$ gives 7.85, so I is true. In water $Cu^{2+}$ is the more stable ion, so II is false. The radii are about 73 pm for $Cu^{2+}$ and 77 pm for $Cu^{+}$, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the 3p effective nuclear charges of these species. I. The 3p electrons of $Ca^{2+}$ feel a higher value than those of $K^{+}$. II. The 3p electrons of Ar feel a lower value than those of $Ca^{2+}$. III. The 3p electrons of $K^{+}$ feel a lower value than those of Ar. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Ca^{2+}$ gives 8.75 and $K^{+}$ gives 7.75, so I is true. Ar gives 6.75, which is lower than $Ca^{2+}$ at 8.75, so II is true. $K^{+}$ gives 7.75, which is higher than Ar at 6.75, so III is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of a $Cu^{+}$ ion (Z = 29, $[Ar]3d^{10}$). What percentage of the nuclear charge is screened from one 3d electron, rounded to the nearest whole percent?
questions.explanation: The nine partner 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $3.15$, and the eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $21.15$, and $21.15/29 = 0.729$, which rounds to 73 percent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the acid-base character of the Group 13 oxides. I. $Al_2O_3$ is amphoteric. II. $B_2O_3$ is amphoteric. III. $Al_2O_3$ is more basic than $B_2O_3$. Which option is correct?
questions.explanation: $Al_2O_3$ reacts with both acids and strong bases, so I is true. $B_2O_3$ is acidic rather than amphoteric, so II is false. $Al_2O_3$ is more basic than $B_2O_3$, which is strongly acidic, so III is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Iron has successive ionisation enthalpies of 762 kJ/mol (IE1) and 1562 kJ/mol (IE2). Divide IE2 by IE1 and report the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The ratio is $1562/762 = 2.05$, which rounds to 2. The second electron is removed at roughly twice the energy of the first.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge felt by one electron of a $Ni^{2+}$ ion (Z = 28, $[Ar]3d^8$), using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The seven other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $20.45$, so $Z_{eff} = 28 - 20.45 = 7.55$. Quoting the Ni neutral 4s value gives 4.05, copying the Cu2+ value gives 8.20, and reporting the total screening gives 20.45.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 3d effective nuclear charges of selected ions, estimated with standard screening constants. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{2+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Mn^{2+}$, about $6.25$ against $5.60$.
B) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{3+}$ feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{2+}$, about $6.60$ against $8.20$.
C) The 3d electrons of $Cr^{3+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Ti^{3+}$, about $5.30$ against $4.00$.
D) The 3d electrons of $Cu^{+}$ feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Cu^{2+}$, about $7.85$ against $8.20$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using electronegativities and ionisation enthalpies of d-block and neighbouring elements, which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using standard textbook values.
options: A) Cu (Pauling 1.90) is more electronegative than Fe (Pauling 1.83).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of Zn (906 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Cu (745 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ca (590 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Sc (633 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Mn (717 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Fe (762 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Cu $(1.90)$ is above Fe $(1.83)$, so A is correct. Zn $(906)$ is above Cu $(745)$, so B is correct. Ca $(590)$ is below Sc $(633)$ because the rising nuclear charge outweighs the poor shielding of the added 3d electron, so C is false. Mn $(717)$ is below Fe $(762)$, so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the stability of oxidation states in Group 14 and Group 15 elements, which reflect the inert pair effect and related trends. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) $Pb^{2+}$ is more stable than $Pb^{4+}$ in aqueous solution.
B) $Sn^{4+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Sn^{2+}$.
D) The electron gain enthalpy of N is more negative than that of O.
questions.explanation: The inert pair effect makes $Pb^{2+}$ more stable than $Pb^{4+}$, so A is correct. $Sn^{2+}$ is the reducing form, so B is false. $Bi^{5+}$ is a strong oxidant, so $Bi^{3+}$ is the stable ion, making C correct. Nitrogen's electron gain enthalpy is near zero or positive, far less negative than oxygen's (-141), so D is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Cu^{2+}$ (Z = 29) and of $Ti^{3+}$ (Z = 22), using the usual screening conventions. Divide the first value by the second and round the ratio to the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a $Co^{2+}$ ion (Z = 27, $[Ar]3d^7$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The six other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.10$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $18.00$. Total screening is $20.10$, so $Z_{eff} = 27 - 20.10 = 6.90$. Quoting the $Fe^{2+}$ value gives 6.25, quoting the $Ni^{2+}$ value gives 7.55, and reporting total screening gives 20.10.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Consider the 4s and 3d effective nuclear charges of selected atoms and ions. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply, using usual screening conventions.
options: A) The 4s electrons of Ti (about $3.15$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Ca (about $2.85$).
B) The 3d electrons of Zn (about $8.85$) feel a lower effective nuclear charge than those of Ti (about $3.65$).
C) The 3d electrons of $Fe^{2+}$ (about $6.25$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of $Co^{2+}$ (about $6.90$).
D) The 3d electrons of Ti (about $3.65$) feel a higher effective nuclear charge than those of Sc (about $3.00$).
questions.explanation: Ti 4s gives $22 - 18.85 = 3.15$, above Ca 4s at $20 - 17.15 = 2.85$, so A is correct. Zn 3d gives $30 - 21.15 = 8.85$, which is higher, not lower, than Ti 3d at $22 - 18.35 = 3.65$, so B is false. $Fe^{2+}$ at 6.25 is lower than $Co^{2+}$ at 6.90, so C is false. Ti 3d at 3.65 exceeds Sc 3d at $21 - 18.00 = 3.00$, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compare the Pauling electronegativities and first ionisation enthalpies of Group 13 and Group 14 elements. Which of the following statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: A) The Pauling electronegativity of Ga (1.81) exceeds that of Al (1.61).
B) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ga (579 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Al (578 kJ/mol).
C) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ge (762 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Si (787 kJ/mol).
D) The first ionisation enthalpy of Ge (762 kJ/mol) exceeds that of Sn (708 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Ga $(1.81)$ is above Al $(1.61)$, so A is correct. Ga's IE1 of $579$ kJ/mol is just above Al's $578$ kJ/mol because the $3d^{10}$ electrons shield poorly, so B is correct. Ge $(762)$ is below Si $(787)$, so C is false. Ge $(762)$ is above Sn $(708)$, so D is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Count how many of the following statements are correct. (i) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Mn^{2+}$. (ii) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Co^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Fe^{2+}$. (iii) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Ti^{3+}$ exceeds that of $Cr^{3+}$. (iv) The 3d effective nuclear charge of $Cu^{2+}$ exceeds that of $Zn^{2+}$.
questions.explanation: $Fe^{2+}$ (6.25) exceeds $Mn^{2+}$ (5.60), so (i) is correct. $Co^{2+}$ (6.90) exceeds $Fe^{2+}$ (6.25), so (ii) is correct. $Ti^{3+}$ (4.00) is below $Cr^{3+}$ (5.30), so (iii) is false. $Zn^{2+}$ (8.85) exceeds $Cu^{2+}$ (8.20), so (iv) is false. Two statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge experienced by the 4s electron of a neutral vanadium atom (Z = 23, $[Ar]3d^3 4s^2$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The partner 4s electron screens $0.35$. The eleven 3s, 3p and 3d electrons screen $0.85$ each for $9.35$, and the ten 1s, 2s and 2p electrons screen $1.00$ each for $10.00$. Total screening is $19.70$, so $Z_{eff} = 23 - 19.70 = 3.30$. Copying the titanium value gives 3.15, ignoring the 3d electrons gives 5.85, and reporting total screening gives 19.70.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3p electron of the $Sc^{3+}$ ion (Z = 21), which carries eighteen electrons in its ground state, $[Ar]$, using the usual screening conventions.
questions.explanation: The seven partner 3s/3p electrons screen $0.35$ each for $2.45$. The eight 2s/2p electrons screen $0.85$ each for $6.80$, and the 1s pair screens $2.00$. Total screening is $11.25$, so $Z_{eff} = 21 - 11.25 = 9.75$. Copying the argon value gives 6.75, ignoring the 1s screening gives 11.75, and reporting total screening gives 11.25.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Compute the ratio of the 3p effective nuclear charge of $Sc^{3+}$ to that of neutral argon, using usual screening conventions. Round the ratio to the nearest integer.
questions.explanation: The $Sc^{3+}$ 3p value is $21 - 11.25 = 9.75$ and the argon 3p value is $18 - 11.25 = 6.75$. The ratio $9.75/6.75 = 1.44$ rounds to 1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Estimate the effective nuclear charge felt by one 3d electron of a neutral chromium atom (Z = 24, $[Ar]3d^5 4s^1$), using the usual screening conventions. Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: The four other 3d electrons screen $0.35$ each for $1.40$. The eighteen inner electrons screen $1.00$ each for $18.00$. Total screening is $19.40$, so $Z_{eff} = 24 - 19.40 = 4.60$. Quoting the $Mn^{2+}$ value gives 5.60, quoting the $Fe^{2+}$ value gives 6.25, and reporting total screening gives 19.40.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Divide the 3d effective nuclear charge of $Fe^{3+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^5$) by that of $Fe^{2+}$ (Z = 26, $[Ar]3d^6$), using the usual screening conventions, and round the ratio to the nearest integer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: Using Pauling electronegativities of 1.81 for Ga and 3.16 for Cl, estimate the percentage ionic character of the GaCl bond, rounded to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The difference is $\Delta\chi = 3.16 - 1.81 = 1.35$, so $\Delta\chi^2/4 = 1.8225/4 = 0.456$. The ionic character is $100(1 - e^{-0.456}) = 100(1 - 0.634) = 36.6$, which rounds to 37. Quoting the covalent fraction gives 63, skipping the square gives 19, and reporting the raw difference as a percentage gives 1.35.
